title: Day 3 PSM — Section 1
subject: Community Medicine
description: FMGE Community Medicine practice from the reviewed Day 3 PSM question bank, section 1 of 4.

questions.stem: A child has low weight-for-height but normal height-for-age. This indicates:
questions.explanation: Low weight-for-height indicates wasting and acute malnutrition. Normal height-for-age argues against the stunting pattern.

questions.stem: Birth weight normally triples by:
questions.explanation: Birth weight approximately doubles by five months and triples by one year.

questions.stem: An Anganwadi worker measures MUAC of 11.2 cm in a 2-year-old. What should she do?
questions.explanation: A MUAC of 11.2 cm meets the severe criterion. Referral is appropriate; feeding advice alone does not complete the response.

questions.stem: For a student in Class VII, the school meal programme’s daily energy norm is:
questions.explanation: Class VII is upper primary, for which the listed meal energy norm is 700 kcal; 450 kcal applies to primary classes.

questions.stem: The predominant immunoglobulin in human milk is:
questions.explanation: Secretory IgA is the predominant immunoglobulin in human milk.

questions.stem: Blood donated at a camp is screened for HIV before transfusion. This is:
questions.explanation: Screening donated blood protects the eventual recipient, fitting prospective screening. Prescriptive screening primarily benefits the person tested.

questions.stem: Identify the instrument shown.
questions.image_alt: Horizontal measuring board with a sliding end piece
questions.image_source: p.10 | lower-central photograph of the horizontal measuring board only; crop excludes the handwritten title
questions.explanation: An infantometer is a horizontal board for measuring an infant’s length. The Salter scale is the hanging weighing instrument.

questions.stem: At one sitting, each factory worker has a blood-pressure measurement, a blood-glucose test and a vision test. Giving several different tests at one sitting is called:
questions.explanation: Giving several different tests at one sitting makes screening multiphasic. Selective screening targets a high-risk group, whatever tests it uses.

questions.stem: A used plastic urinary catheter is collected for biomedical-waste disposal. After treatment, its final pathway is:
questions.explanation: A used plastic catheter follows the red-category treatment pathway and is then recycled.

questions.stem: Low height-for-age in a child is termed:
questions.explanation: Low height-for-age indicates stunting; wasting uses weight-for-height.

questions.stem: A test finds 90 true positives, 10 false negatives, 20 false positives and 80 true negatives. Its sensitivity is:
questions.explanation: Sensitivity is \(90/(90+10)\times100=90\%\). False positives and true negatives are outside its denominator.

questions.stem: A rural ICDS project, headed by a Child Development Project Officer, covers which administrative unit?
questions.explanation: The ICDS project operates at block level, with a Child Development Project Officer in charge.

questions.stem: Three readings are 150/90, 150/90 and 150/90 mmHg; the reference is 120/80 mmHg. They are:
questions.explanation: The identical readings are precise. Their distance from the reference value makes them inaccurate.

questions.stem: Generalizability of study results to other settings reflects:
questions.explanation: External validity asks whether results apply in other settings. Internal validity concerns the trustworthiness of results within the study.

questions.stem: At a flood-relief camp, free residual chlorine is 0.1 mg/L one hour after water treatment. The next action is:
questions.explanation: A residual of 0.1 mg/L is inadequate after treatment. Additional chlorine is needed before the supply is accepted.

questions.stem: All of the following are suitable for biomedical-waste incineration EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: PVC-containing waste is listed as unsuitable for incineration. The other listed wastes have incineration pathways.

questions.stem: Discarded metallic implants enter which biomedical-waste colour category?
questions.explanation: Discarded metallic implants belong in the blue category; sharps such as needles and blades belong in white.

questions.stem: Ten hours after an earthquake, teams arrange casualty transport and sanitation. This belongs to which relief phase?
questions.explanation: The secondary follow-up phase covers 6–24 hours and includes transport and sanitation work.

questions.stem: Autoclaving sterilizes by:
questions.explanation: An autoclave uses steam under pressure. Dry heat is a separate sterilization approach.

questions.stem: A water sample has hardness due to calcium bicarbonate. Which household measure reduces it?
questions.explanation: Bicarbonate hardness is temporary and can be reduced by boiling. Chlorination addresses disinfection.

questions.stem: Under CPCB’s National Air Quality Index, an AQI of 250 is classified as:
questions.explanation: An AQI of 250 falls within the poor band of 201–300.

questions.stem: The capacity of a health system to expand its disaster response is:
questions.explanation: Surge capacity is the health system’s ability to respond when disaster demand rises.

questions.stem: Light incident on a classroom desk is measured in:
questions.explanation: Illuminance at the desk is measured in lux. Lumen is the unit of luminous flux.

questions.stem: Domestic liquid waste without human excreta is:
questions.explanation: Sullage is domestic liquid waste without human excreta; sewage includes it.

questions.stem: A worker checks free residual chlorine in treated drinking water. Which instrument is used?
questions.explanation: A chloroscope checks free residual chlorine in treated water. Horrocks apparatus addresses chlorine demand before dosing.

questions.stem: Dengue cases are rising in a ward. Which source-reduction measure targets the main vector’s breeding site?
questions.explanation: Removing water from containers targets the breeding sites of Aedes mosquitoes. Clearing dirty drains targets a different breeding pattern.

questions.stem: The vector of onchocerciasis is the:
questions.explanation: Onchocerciasis is transmitted by the black fly. Sand flies transmit the leishmaniases listed separately.

questions.stem: Compared with cow’s milk, human milk has a higher proportion of:
questions.explanation: Human milk has more lactose, whereas cow’s milk has a higher casein proportion.
